A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mono-InternVL and EViP. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.4 are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original multimodal benchmark results, pre-training evaluations, ablations, inference measurements, and qualitative examples, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations on four language-only benchmarks in Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same patch/thumbnail tokenizer, statically routed visual and textual experts, expert initialization, autoregressive objective, three-stage EViP freezing schedule, and full-model instruction tuning. No architectural or algorithmic revision is established.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMLU, CMMLU, AGIEval, and MATH evaluation while retaining the 16 multimodal benchmarks. Section 3.3 and Appendix Table 7 remove the reported video and handwritten instruction-data categories. Table 7 also replaces captioning ShareGPT-4o with ShareGPT4V and conversation ShareGPT with TextOCR-GPT4V; text-only ShareGPT remains. These substantially revise documented training and evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The shared multimodal comparison adds Qwen2VL-2B and removes MobileVLM-V2-1.7B and MiniCPM-V, while retaining their larger/newer variants. The new NLP comparison includes InternLM2-Chat alongside EVE and Chameleon. Emu3 already appeared in v1 and is not a new baseline.

E3.justification: The new NLP experiment uses OpenCompass for Mono-InternVL, InternLM2-Chat, and EVE, with Chameleon explicitly excepted. Existing multimodal benchmark splits, normalization, patch budgets, training configurations, ablation procedures, and latency settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds a language-retention check against InternLM2-Chat, addressing a property previously supported indirectly through multimodal experiments. The visual-expert and delta-tuning ablations, attention-freezing study, scaling curves, attention maps, and appendix examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point scores and task averages without seed counts, repeated-run information, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. The new NLP results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: The new NLP results materially extend evidence concerning language retention: Mono-InternVL scores 45.1, 44.0, 40.9, and 12.3 on MMLU, CMMLU, AGIEval, and MATH, respectively, with comparator results in Table 4. Qwen2VL scores are added and two older comparator rows disappear. Retained multimodal, pre-training, ablation, efficiency, and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6) retain the same mathematical definitions and objective. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations beyond the shared formulation.

C1.justification: v1 claims state-of-the-art results on six multimodal benchmarks and emphasizes leading performance without a pretrained visual encoder. v2 narrows the modular comparison to comparable performance and redirects headline superiority toward monolithic competitors, claiming wins on 13 of 16 benchmarks and highlighting Emu3. This substantially changes the performance contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v1 attributes high-resolution weaknesses to unoptimized positional embeddings and training data; v2 instead tentatively attributes them to shallow model depth. v2 also interprets the new NLP results as evidence of language retention and suggests better instruction data and a stronger LLM could close the Qwen2VL gap.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code/model release announcement and direct Hugging Face access link beyond the retained project page. It specifies the caption generator as InternVL2-8B rather than InternVL-8B; the PDFs do not establish whether this corrects the name or reflects changed caption generation. Appendix Table 8's hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Qwen2-VL, the NLP benchmarks, ShareGPT4V, TextOCR-GPT4V, and the already-compared Flamingo, while removing references associated with omitted video and handwriting datasets. It positions InternVL-1.5 as a matched modular counterpart and emphasizes Emu3 within the retained modular/monolithic/MoE framing.

P1.justification: The abstract and portions of the introduction and comparative discussion are rewritten, the modular related-work paragraph is shortened, an author and affiliation are added, and citations become numerical. The section sequence and most method and appendix prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting changes typography, margins, headers, caption placement, and display sizing. v1 Tables 2 and 3 merge into a dense, wide v2 Table 2, and a new NLP Table 4 appears. Other tables and appendix displays are restyled or repositioned; Figures 1–6 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The NLP comparison directly examines a central language-retention claim previously supported indirectly, while Qwen2VL and narrower modular claims improve empirical positioning. These benefits support a limited improvement despite new reporting errors: Table 2 supports 12 of 16 monolithic wins and 8 of 12 against Emu3, contradicting v2's stated 13 of 16 and 9 of 12.
